title: MIPI UniPro data link layer: 8-bit serial symbols, COF / ESC_DL framing, CRC-16, data frames with ACK / NAC, resend on timeout, TC0 / TC1 priority queues, PACP GET / SET of 16 attributes, a CPort 0 message buffer

words.name: TC0
words.desc: push one 32-bit payload onto the TC0 transmit queue (8 entries; a push to a full queue is dropped with ERR)

words.name: TC1
words.desc: push one 32-bit payload onto the TC1 transmit queue (strict priority over TC0)

words.name: PACP_SET
words.desc: PACP SET request to the peer: [15:8] value, [3:0] attribute index

words.name: PACP_GET
words.desc: PACP GET request to the peer: [3:0] attribute index

words.name: CPORT
words.desc: [3:0] destination CPort of the following pushes

words.name: MSG
words.desc: [7:0] next message-buffer byte (CPort 0 payloads, 32 bytes); the read pops it

words.name: STATUS
words.desc: {pacp_cnf, pacp_rsp_valid, tx busy, PACP request pending, data frame outstanding, resends[1:0], control FIFO count[2:0], rx expected seq[3:0], tx seq[3:0], msg count[5:0], TC1 count[3:0], TC0 count[3:0]}

words.name: PACP
words.desc: {pacp_cnf, pacp_rsp_valid, GET response value[7:0]}; the read clears both flags

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: received CRC / length error or framing error, message buffer overflow, control FIFO overflow, resend budget exhausted, or a push to a full queue

notes: rx_bit / tx_bit (start + 8 data bits LSB first + stop, idle 1, one bit per PCLK) pass through unchanged.
The core's CPU port is mapped one word per register; a write with PSTRB != 4'hF to a writable word is dropped with PSLVERR.
